name: find the letter a printed text never uses
one_line: A short story missing one letter of the alphabet, the alphabet printed beneath it to tick off, and three lines to try it.
how: Compose the text by hand and then count it by hand: the forbidden letter zero times, and every other letter of the alphabet present at least once. Without that second condition the question has more than one answer and the sheet is broken. Seventy words is enough. Print the alphabet under it as a row of letters to be ticked off while a finger runs along the text: that row is the checker, and without it the search runs from memory and never ends. Then ask what else went missing — in Italian a text with no R has no infinitive — and only after that ask for three lines written under the same rule, saying they need not be good. Anything that does not read letters one at a time returns a text of the right shape that breaks its own rule, so it must be counted before it is printed.

knobs.knob: handed over as a puzzle or as a task
knobs.effect: As a task, writing under a letter rule from cold is refused. As an absence to be noticed it gets read, and the three lines of writing come after somebody has already seen what the rule does to a sentence.

A rare consonant is invisible and there is nothing to notice. A frequent one bends every line. A letter carrying a whole grammatical class — R in Italian — takes the infinitive with it, which is the discovery worth having and what makes composing hard.
Printed, the search is finite and ends in two minutes, mechanically. Left out, it is an open hunt with no stopping rule, and somebody who has the right answer has no way of knowing they do.

knobs.knob: never using it or striking it out
knobs.effect: Never using the letter leaves a readable text with a hole in it. Deleting it from the words that had it leaves a text to be deciphered, which is reconstruction and not noticing: a different exercise under the same name.

where_the_work_is: In the text being fixed material, composed and counted once and then printed for ever. None of it can be produced at the moment of delivery, and a text nobody counted makes the question unanswerable.
breaks: It fails quietly: a text that looks right and uses the forbidden letter twice makes the ticking row contradict itself, and nothing downstream notices. The three written lines are checked by nobody, which is right — they are a first try and not a submission. On 800x480 a seventy-word text and an alphabet do not both fit, and the alphabet is the half that does the work.
